## What this session actually did

Three questions were asked of the archive rather than of the literature, and
the answers are what the night produced.

**Mid-generation signals for overthinking.** About forty records bear on this;
they sort into five families (trial-answer confidence, hidden-state probes,
entropy, lexical/behavioural markers, answer convergence). Two are deployable
and three are not, and the reason turned out to be shared. That became
`finding:11877d6cb7defd0d`: a signal predicts only when it carries temporal
structure. It is filed against six papers including the one that contradicts
the intuition hardest — *Amplified Does Not Mean Predictive*, where expressed
uncertainty carries negative Lift.

**Analyses of overthinking behaviour inside the trace.** About twenty records,
in four methodological groups: hand-read failure taxonomies, length-accuracy
dissections, causal interventions (only three papers), and benchmark-anchored
studies. The thinnest part is agentic evidence — one paper, with the largest
effect size of any of them (R² = 0.892), and nothing reproducing it. That is
now queued as `synthesis__q-85150997e2cfc3ad`.

**A staged argument built from both.** Written into
`wiki/topics/overthinking.md` below `<!-- auto:end -->`, declared at 21
sources. It asks whether allocation tracks difficulty or presentation, walks
six stages of archive evidence, and concludes that the deficit is in the
signal allocation is conditioned on rather than in the ability to allocate —
because the decision is fixed at read time, when only presentation is
available. Three predictions it makes are checked against the archive and
hold; five things that would overturn it are listed with it.

The section is the first here to carry an `analysis-sources` marker, so render
will report it stale once the evidence doubles.

## Correction and continuation, later the same day

Two statements above were written before the work they describe was done, and
one of them is wrong.

**"The template is eight commits ahead again" is wrong — it was 120.** Eight was
what the first screen of `git log HEAD..src/main` showed. The real count matters
because of what the rest of it contained: upstream had moved its own archive to a
repository of its own, so `src/main` no longer tracks `data/`, `archive/` or
`outputs/`, and a plain `git merge src/main` would have proposed deleting the
4,418 files this deployment keeps there. The merge was done instead as `-s ours`
plus an explicit checkout of the code trees; see
`docs/commit-local/0036-taking-the-template-back-in-a-second-time.md`.

**The four papers have now been read**, so the caution about trusting the
`wiki/topics/overthinking.md` argument before reading them is discharged. Two of
them bear on it directly and both support it. $R^3$-Bench is the strongest
single piece of evidence the argument has: because its oracle is built from each
model's own isolated successes, its 71-of-72-cell shortfall cannot be read as a
capability limit, and it separates the two tails by budget pressure -- "spent
budget elsewhere" dominates under strong pressure, "stopped after partial
progress" under moderate. *Learning When to Think* supplies the counterexample
the argument lacked: its two-mode precursor collapsed on Countdown because that
task's uniform difficulty gives a router no accuracy gap to learn from, which
makes difficulty routing a property of the training distribution rather than of
the model. Neither changes the conclusion, so the `analysis-sources` count stays
at 21 rather than being restated; the next revision of that section should fold
them in and raise it.

The other two are honestly tangential and are recorded as such. EchoCoT is a
security paper whose only use here is external evidence on frontier hidden-trace
lengths and on what those traces contain. The edge-RAG paper is a systems paper
whose one transferable idea is methodological: it charges the compressor's own
latency and energy against the savings, and finds a regime where compression
makes every configuration worse. Almost no efficiency method in this archive is
reported that way.

**What the merge brought, and what it cost.** The `model` wiki kind, the
authored alias map, an entity-split report, a keyword-overlap check, dated
listing records and eight maintenance scripts. The keyword check immediately
found a real defect in `config/topics/overthinking.yaml` -- `reasoning token` and
`reasoning-token` both listed, scoring the same words twice -- now deleted.
Applying the alias map retired 20 concept records and took `fragmented` from 12
to zero. It also cost: four definitions were cleared because each had been
written against a fraction of its merged entity's evidence, and a fifth of the
queue turned out to be definition tasks for entities the map had already
retired, which is fixed in
`docs/commit-local/0037-a-ruling-takes-the-question-with-it.md`.

**The queue is at zero.** 4 papers, 26 concept definitions and the synthesis
question were answered. The synthesis question was answered *open*, which is the
part worth reading: the archive cannot say whether agentic overthinking is the
same phenomenon the maths benchmarks measure, because the one record spanning
both settings runs maths problems in both arms and so shares the phenomenon by
construction. What would settle it is one measurement applying both instruments
to one set of trajectories, and nothing here has ever done that.

**Still open.** 22 definitions their evidence has outgrown, drained five per
render by design. 277 readings name no model, which the `model` kind now reports
every pass and `scripts/backfill_summary_models.py` exists to fix. And the
listing records still carry no date.
